rows.selected_title: HBV/HCV coinfection and anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury: from risk assessment and exploration of mechanisms to preventive considerations.
rows.title: HBV/HCV coinfection and anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury: from risk assessment and exploration of mechanisms to preventive considerations.
rows.abstract: Anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (AT-DILI) is a common and clinically significant adverse event during tuberculosis treatment. Previous studies have frequently reported an increased risk of AT-DILI among patients coinfected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) and/or hepatitis C virus (HCV). This review aims to explore potential mechanisms underlying this heightened susceptibility and to discuss prevention considerations for patients with tuberculosis and HBV/HCV coinfection. We conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, supplemented by clinical guidelines and authoritative reports, to identify relevant studies published through August 2026. Relevant articles were screened and thematically organized to synthesize evidence on risk estimation, underlying mechanisms, and prevention considerations. Available evidence indicates that HBV/HCV coinfection is associated with increased AT-DILI risk, with the magnitude varying by viral activity, baseline liver disease, and virological indicator selection. Higher viral loads appear more closely associated with AT-DILI risk. Potential mechanisms include immune-inflammatory changes, altered drug metabolism, reduced hepatic reserve, and virus-specific liver injury, including HBV reactivation. These observations inform preventive strategies targeting these risks and potential mechanisms, including baseline hepatic and virological assessment, dynamic monitoring, antiviral therapy, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimen optimization, and selective use of hepatoprotective agents. HBV/HCV coinfection increases the risk of AT-DILI and warrants active clinical attention. Future efforts should focus on individualizing prevention based on virological and hepatic status, while validating emerging biomarkers and artificial intelligence-based predictive tools to refine risk identification.

rows.selected_title: An integrated framework for clinical surveillance in multiple sclerosis: An evidence-informed narrative review.
rows.title: An integrated framework for clinical surveillance in multiple sclerosis: An evidence-informed narrative review.
rows.abstract: An Integrated Framework for Clinical Surveillance in Multiple Sclerosis: an evidenceinformed narrative review Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) requires structured lifelong surveillance across clinical, imaging, safety and patient-centred domains. We aimed to integrate relevant recommendations and evidence into a practical framework for longitudinal care. We conducted an evidence-informed narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library from inception to December 2025, supplemented by society and institutional guidance and reference-list searching. Evidence was synthesised across clinical and cognitive assessment, neuroimaging, laboratory safety monitoring, emerging biomarkers, treatment escalation and de-escalation, vaccination, reproductive health, and a tiered minimal core monitoring set. No formal risk-of-bias assessment or evidence grading was performed. The proposed framework integrates clinical and cognitive measures, conventional MRI and drug-specific safety monitoring. NEDA-3 is adopted as the operational treat-to-target framework; NEDA-4 and biomarker-enhanced composites are discussed as emerging extensions. Serum neurofilament light chain and glial fibrillary acidic protein provide complementary prognostic information but do not independently identify progression independent of relapse activity or mandate treatment escalation. Confirmed inflammatory activity is distinguished from disability accumulation and adjunctive biomarker or quantitative imaging signals. Vaccination, reproductive health and symptomatic management are incorporated alongside authorproposed essential, recommended and advanced monitoring tiers. This framework is intended to support coordinated, risk-adapted MS surveillance. Its operational recommendations and monitoring tiers require prospective validation, and implementation should reflect patient characteristics, treatment-specific requirements and local resources.

rows.selected_title: Spatial scaffolds or spatial dependency? A structured evidence map of AR/MR interfaces for piano learning and practice.
rows.title: Spatial scaffolds or spatial dependency? A structured evidence map of AR/MR interfaces for piano learning and practice.
rows.abstract: Augmented- and mixed-reality (AR/MR) systems for piano learning and practice provide spatially aligned key highlights, piano-roll cues, virtual hands, performance feedback, and gamified guidance. Previous reviews have already identified unresolved questions concerning sight-reading, cognitive load, retention, transfer, and the possibility of interface dependence. The present review therefore does not treat these issues as previously unrecognized research gaps. Instead, it provides a structured evidence map of empirical studies of AR/MR and spatially augmented interfaces for piano learning and practice and examines how interface design relates to the kinds of learning outcomes that have been measured. Backward and forward citation tracking, supplemented by open bibliographic metadata and publisher searches, identified 36 candidate records. After two duplicate, expanded, or preliminary reports were removed or merged, 34 records were screened, 20 reports underwent detailed eligibility assessment, and 18 empirical reports were retained in the core evidence map. The reports were coded according to two dimensions: notation continuity-notation-preserving, notation-bridging, and notation-replacing interfaces-and scaffold withdrawal-persistent, contingent, progressively faded, or removed guidance. The evidence is strongest for proximal outcomes, including immediate note accuracy, task completion, usability, engagement, motivation, and perceived workload. A smaller number of studies examined repeated practice, motor-skill development, or performance after guidance was reduced or removed. However, delayed unaided transfer to conventional staff notation remains weakly tested. The available evidence therefore indicates that spatial guidance can provide effective immediate task support but does not establish that it consistently produces independent music-reading skills or that it necessarily creates dependency. The review's contribution lies in linking notation continuity, scaffold withdrawal, and outcome distance to clarify what existing studies can-and cannot-demonstrate about learning.

rows.selected_title: From Ion to Iron: A Focused Narrative Literature Review of Magnesium Supplementation for Muscle Strength and Recovery.
rows.title: From Ion to Iron: A Focused Narrative Literature Review of Magnesium Supplementation for Muscle Strength and Recovery.
rows.abstract: Magnesium is an essential mineral involved in numerous physiological processes, including energy metabolism, neuromuscular function, protein synthesis, and inflammatory regulation. Given these roles, magnesium supplementation has received increasing attention as a potential strategy to support exercise performance and recovery. This review aimed to evaluate the current evidence regarding magnesium intake and its effects on exercise performance, skeletal muscle recovery, body composition, and inflammatory responses. A focused narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed to identify studies published between 2000 and 2025 that contained the terms "magnesium" and "muscle" in the title. Review articles, meta-analyses, animal studies, commentaries, guidelines, and studies lacking clinical muscle-related outcomes were excluded. Outcomes of interest included exercise performance, recovery measures, body composition, and inflammatory markers. Of 108 records identified, 10 studies met inclusion criteria, including six randomized controlled trials and four observational studies. Evidence regarding exercise performance was inconsistent. Some randomized trials demonstrated improvements in muscular strength, functional mobility, perceived exertion, and repetitions to failure, whereas others reported no performance benefit or reductions in maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max) and sprint power with higher-dose supplementation. Recovery-related outcomes were generally more favorable, with several studies reporting reduced muscle soreness, improved perceived recovery, and lower markers of exercise-induced muscle damage. Magnesium intake was also associated with lower concentrations of inflammatory biomarkers, including high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interleukin-6. Observational studies consistently demonstrated associations between higher dietary magnesium intake and greater skeletal muscle mass, improved body composition, and lower systemic inflammation. Current evidence suggests that magnesium supplementation may provide greater benefit for exercise recovery and inflammatory regulation than for direct enhancement of athletic performance. Variability in study design, magnesium formulation, supplementation dose, participant characteristics, and baseline magnesium status likely contributed to the inconsistent performance findings observed across studies. Magnesium supplementation may be most appropriately considered an adjunct recovery-support strategy rather than a primary ergogenic aid. Large, well-designed randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify optimal dosing strategies, identify populations most likely to benefit, and further elucidate the mechanisms through which magnesium influences muscle function and exercise adaptation.

rows.selected_title: Persistent and recurrent musculoskeletal pain in young athletes: an overlooked biopsychosocial determinant of return to sport trajectories - a focused narrative review.
rows.title: Persistent and recurrent musculoskeletal pain in young athletes: an overlooked biopsychosocial determinant of return to sport trajectories - a focused narrative review.
rows.abstract: Persistent and recurrent musculoskeletal pain is common in young athletes, yet its role in recovery and return to sport (RTS) decision-making remains insufficiently acknowledged. In youth sport, pain is often normalized or viewed primarily through an injury-centered lens, despite its potential to shape function, participation patterns, and athletic trajectories over time. This focused narrative review aimed to (1) synthesize current evidence on persistent and recurrent musculoskeletal pain in young athletes and (2) propose a developmentally informed biopsychosocial framework for understanding its implications for RTS. Electronic searches were conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO, and SPORTDiscus for studies published from 1 January 2006, through 28 February 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking and targeted hand-searching of reference lists. It integrates evidence on definitions, prevalence, clinical presentation, psychosocial and contextual factors, functional interference, and RTS decision-making, conceptualizing ongoing pain as an overlooked determinant of RTS trajectories. In young athletes, pain should not be treated as a peripheral symptom or addressed only when recovery is delayed. More informed RTS decisions require attention not only to physical recovery markers, but also to how pain is experienced, interpreted, and managed throughout recovery. A developmentally informed biopsychosocial perspective may support earlier recognition, safer return decisions, more stable participation, and better long-term health outcomes.

rows.selected_title: Microglial GPR56 in synaptic pruning: mechanisms, comparative receptor biology, and context-dependent roles in brain disorders.
rows.title: Microglial GPR56 in synaptic pruning: mechanisms, comparative receptor biology, and context-dependent roles in brain disorders.
rows.abstract: Microglia regulate synaptic remodelling, eliminating weakened and dysfunctional synapses to maintain circuit development and homeostasis. Adhesion G protein-coupled receptor G1 (ADGRG1/GPR56) has emerged as a distinctive regulator integrating phosphatidylserine recognition, mechano-transduction, and G-protein signalling. This review synthesises the molecular, cellular and disease-level evidence, distinguishing throughout between direct experimental findings, associations, and proposed mechanisms. We discuss its structural organisation, the microglia-enriched splice variant 4 (S4), and how phosphatidylserine-exposing synapses are recognised and engulfed. The Gα12/13-RhoA cascade placed downstream of microglial GPR56 was defined in neural progenitor cells and has not been perturbed in microglia; it is presented as proposed rather than established. Comparison with CR3, CX3CR1, TREM2, MERTK, MEGF10 and BAI1, identifies microglia-enriched alternative splicing, direct coupling of phosphatidylserine recognition to G-protein signalling, and mechanosensitivity as distinguishing features. We then evaluate evidence linking GPR56 to traumatic brain injury, major depressive disorder, maternal immune activation models, and Alzheimer's disease. In every context the causal evidence is loss-of-function: removing the receptor worsens the phenotype, including in Alzheimer's disease, where microglial ADGRG1 is increased yet deletion aggravates amyloid pathology and cognitive decline. The evidence supports a protective receptor that, when lost, produces different outputs in different settings, not one that switches between protective and pathological roles. The four disease outcomes are different from each other and from developmental pruning. The idea that they all involve a single S4-dependent mechanism remains a hypothesis, not a confirmed fact. We conclude by discussing therapeutic and biomarker opportunities and translational challenges.

rows.selected_title: The impact of intergenerational transmission of stigma on the psychological development of minors with HIV-positive parents.
rows.title: The impact of intergenerational transmission of stigma on the psychological development of minors with HIV-positive parents.
rows.abstract: With the widespread adoption of antiretroviral therapy, HIV infection has become a chronic, manageable condition, and the population of HIV-positive parents continues to grow. The stigma linked to their condition passes down to their minor children within the family. This harms the children's mental health and makes it harder to prevent and control HIV. This review explores the patterns and mechanisms of intergenerational transmission. It uses stigma theory and ecological systems theory. By examining evidence from around the world and within China, it highlights transmission features and how to adapt interventions specifically for the Chinese context. The results indicate that the stigma experienced by HIV-positive parents exhibits three-dimensional overlap, role specificity, and chronic persistence, with significant population heterogeneity. Intergenerational transmission happens through a four-level chain. It includes family communication and disclosure, parent-child attachment, and family functioning. Next, parental emotions and behaviors come into play. Finally, children's understanding and internalisation of stigma follow. This process shows a dose-response relationship with psychological harm in children. Among existing interventions, family-system-integrated interventions yield the best outcomes, supplemented by individual parental interventions, child protection measures, and social structural interventions; these must be adapted to local cultural and population characteristics. The study shows that we can intervene in the intergenerational passing of disease-related shame. Future research should include longitudinal studies, focus on specific populations, and develop multi-system collaborative intervention models to safeguard the rights of affected children and improve the comprehensive HIV/AIDS prevention and control system.

rows.selected_title: Exploring the Effect of Nutrition on Fetal Development in Pregnant Patients With Inflammatory Gut Diseases: A Scoping Review.
rows.title: Exploring the Effect of Nutrition on Fetal Development in Pregnant Patients With Inflammatory Gut Diseases: A Scoping Review.
rows.abstract: Inflammatory gut diseases (IGDs) are increasing in prevalence and pose unique challenges during pregnancy. Poorly controlled IGDs in pregnant women are linked to adverse fetal outcomes such as low birth weight, preterm birth, and impaired gut microbiome development. Nutritional deficiencies, particularly in magnesium, folate, and vitamin B12, exacerbate these risks due to both inadequate intake and malabsorption. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the role of nutrition in fetal development among pregnant women with IGDs, highlighting dietary strategies that may enhance maternal gastrointestinal health and optimize fetal outcomes. This study was designed as a scoping review to examine the relationship between IGDs, pregnancy, and nutrition. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, a search was conducted for peer-reviewed literature using the databases Embase, Web of Science, Ovid MEDLINE, and CINAHL. The search was restricted to studies published in English within the last ten years and that focused on pregnant or postpartum patients and fetuses in the context of nutrition and IGDs. The search strategy used predefined terms in multiple combinations with Boolean operators: "inflammatory bowel disease", "pregnancy", "fetus development", "nutritional deficiency", "diet restriction", and "vitamin supplementation". The search identified 1,589 records, of which 728 remained after duplicate removal. Following title and abstract screening, 103 full-text reports were sought for retrieval, 98 were assessed for eligibility, and five studies met the final inclusion criteria. The included studies suggest that multidisciplinary antenatal care, maintenance of disease remission, and attention to maternal nutritional status may support favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes. However, the available evidence is limited, consists primarily of observational studies, and no included study directly evaluated nutritional interventions and fetal outcomes. Research on fetal outcomes remains limited and warrants future investigations exploring long-term fetal outcomes, the impact of maternal nutritional deficiencies, and dietary interventions to improve treatment protocols. Advancements in this research can ultimately improve maternal and neonatal outcomes in IGD-affected pregnancies.

rows.selected_title: Precision cognitive neurorehabilitation: dose, adaptivity, digital therapeutics and implementation.
rows.title: Precision cognitive neurorehabilitation: dose, adaptivity, digital therapeutics and implementation.
rows.abstract: Cognitive deficits are determinants of long-term disability and socio-professional reintegration across neurological disorders, including stroke, traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis, and neurodegenerative diseases. Despite evidence supporting cognitive neurorehabilitation, its implementation remains heterogeneous, and therapeutic parameters are insufficiently defined. The authors reviewed the published literature from PubMed and Google Scholar from 1 January 2015 to 30 June 2026, supplemented by seminal publications. Clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational and proof-of-concept studies were prioritized. This brief narrative review examines restorative and compensatory cognitive neurorehabilitation for deficits of attention, executive functions, language and disorders of consciousness in people after stroke and traumatic brain injury (TBI), older adults, and those with neurological and neurodegenerative conditions, including multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. Emphasis is placed on dose, frequency, adaptivity, personalization, and digital and technology-assisted interventions. Methodological challenges include heterogeneity of protocols, limited use of active control conditions, insufficient long-term follow-up, and the gap between cognitive test improvements and meaningful effects on participation. Advancing cognitive neurorehabilitation requires precision-driven approaches integrating digital therapeutics with clinical frameworks. Large-scale pragmatic trials, meaningful endpoints, and implementation strategies across the continuum of care will be essential to transform cognitive neurorehabilitation into a component of neurological practice.

rows.selected_title: An audit of the fracture liaison service at Helen Joseph Tertiary Hospital, Johannesburg, South Africa.
rows.title: An audit of the fracture liaison service at Helen Joseph Tertiary Hospital, Johannesburg, South Africa.
rows.abstract: Fragility fractures are increasing worldwide, yet osteoporosis often remains underdiagnosed and untreated. This study found a high burden of osteoporosis risk factors among patients enrolled in a South African fracture liaison service, highlighting the need for structured secondary prevention. These findings support expansion of fracture liaison services to improve long-term patient outcomes in resource-limited settings. Fragility fractures (FF) driven by osteoporosis result in high morbidity and mortality and are a global health concern. Fracture liaison services (FLSs) are the gold standard for secondary prevention, yet data on their implementation and patient profiles in South Africa remain sparse. The Helen Joseph Tertiary Hospital (HJH) FLS was established to improve this care gap. To describe the clinical and demographic characteristics, risk factors for osteoporosis and falls, osteoporosis risk scores, and management of patients enrolled in the FLS at HJH. This retrospective audit included 247 patients admitted to the orthopaedic ward and enrolled in the FLS between 03 October 2022 and 04 June 2024. Data on demographics, osteoporosis risk factors, investigations and management were analysed. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. The majority of patients were female (74.5%), aged 60-89 years (81.4%). Hip fractures predominated (59.9%), specifically neck of femur (38.8%) and intertrochanteric fractures (21.1%). Although 82.5% of patients received calcium and vitamin D supplementation, only 27.8% received in-hospital bisphosphonate therapy (Zoledronic acid). Medication shortages accounted for 60% of cases in which Zoledronic acid was not administered, while 12.4% were ineligible due to advanced chronic kidney disease. In-hospital mortality was 5%, and median length of stay was 18 days (IQR 11-28). Vitamin D insufficiency was prevalent (41.1%) and did not differ by ethnicity. Significant gender differences were observed: men had substantially higher rates of smoking (73% vs 46%) and alcohol use (48% vs 23%). Inadequate physical activity was a risk factor in both genders. Fall risks included a history of previous falls (42.0%) and cognitive impairment (Mini-Cog <3; 39.6%). Patients with hip fractures had significantly higher FRAX scores than those with fractures at other sites (p < 0.05). This is the first South African Fracture Liaison Service study to report on fall risk, osteoporosis risk, and post-fracture management. Fragility fractures at Helen Joseph Hospital represent a substantial burden, with a high prevalence of clinical risk factors and notable gender-specific contributors, particularly alcohol use in men. While the FLS helps close the treatment gap, its impact is limited by inconsistent access to osteoporosis therapies. Improving outcomes in resource-constrained settings requires reliable medication supply and targeted interventions for fall prevention and modifiable risk factors.

rows.selected_title: Associations Between Hospital Health Information Technology Adoption and Star Ratings, Readmissions, and Mortality.
rows.title: Associations Between Hospital Health Information Technology Adoption and Star Ratings, Readmissions, and Mortality.
rows.abstract: Quality of care is essential to an efficient and cost-effective healthcare system. Health information technology (HIT) adoption has emerged as a promising structural solution for improving the quality of clinical processes and patient outcomes at hospitals. The objective of this work was to estimate the association between hospital HIT adoption and performance on quality indicators (QIs). Cross-sectional study linking data from the 2023 American Hospital Association Annual Survey and Information Technology Supplement, the 2021-2024 Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Hospital Care Compare databases, and the 2023 Area Health Resources Files. Descriptive and regression analyses were run with hospital-level clustering, examining the association between adoption of telehealth (treatment-stage and postdischarge), health information exchange (HIE), and patient engagement (PE) technologies and performance on star ratings (scale of 1-5), 30-day readmissions, and 30-day mortality. Among a sample ranging from 1,636 to 2,771 acute care hospitals in the United States (depending on QI outcome and HIT exposure), telehealth, HIE, and PE adoption were found to be associated with higher star ratings (treatment-stage: 0.36 stars; postdischarge: 0.15 stars; HIE: 0.17 stars; PE: 0.12 stars) and lower mortality (treatment-stage: -0.31 pp.; postdischarge: -0.19 pp.; HIE: -0.19 pp.; PE: -0.16 pp.). HIE adoption was also associated with lower readmissions (-0.07 pp.), whereas the association between PE adoption and readmissions was not statistically significant. Hospital HIT adoption is associated with better performance on QIs, suggesting that digital infrastructure may support hospital quality improvement. Policy efforts should focus on alleviating barriers to adoption and promoting access to technology resources.

rows.selected_title: A Short-Term Longitudinal Study on Arm/Shoulder Functions Following Breast Cancer Surgery and Its Implications on Shoulder Physiotherapy.
rows.title: A Short-Term Longitudinal Study on Arm/Shoulder Functions Following Breast Cancer Surgery and Its Implications on Shoulder Physiotherapy.
rows.abstract: Enhanced survival following breast cancer diagnosis has brought into focus various long term sequelae of treatment, one of the most common of which are arm/shoulder problems (ASPs). To study arm and shoulder functions in the post operative period and early follow up to elucidate the role of surgery in the etiopathogenesis of ASPs and to develop a pragmatic plan for shoulder physiotherapy. This prospective longitudinal study was conducted on (n = 53) patients, who underwent surgery for operable breast cancer. Evaluation of shoulder function was done at 2, 4, and 12 weeks after surgery. Main outcome measures were: (1) Restriction in range of shoulder movement (ROM) assessed using Goniometer; (2) Arm strength measurement using Hand grip dynamometer; (3) Arm/shoulder function assessment using Kwan's Arm Problem scale (KAPS). At 2 weeks, 66% patients showed a significant restriction in flexion and 53% in abduction of shoulder, which had reduced to 7.5% and 9.4% respectively by 12 weeks. Arm strength was significantly reduced at all the three assessments. At 2 weeks, 72% patients had significant arm/shoulder dysfunction (KAPS score > 21.5), while none at 12 weeks. Arm and shoulder pain and use of arm were the items with highest mean scores. Early initiation of structured physiotherapy and an emphasis on both mobility and strength restoration can achieve near complete functional recovery within three months. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13193-026-02548-0.
